title: Resource-level ACLs
description: Each database and record carries its own access-control list naming the identities and groups allowed to reach it. Requests are checked against the ACL of the exact resource requested, so access to one database never implies access to another. ACL changes take effect immediately. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers per-database and per-record access lists.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"db1": ["amy"], "db2": ["bob"]}, 2: {"db1": ["amy", "ops"], "db2": ["bob"]}, 3: {"db1": ["amy", "ops", "auditors"], "db2": ["bob"], "db3": []}}
acls, who, res = CFG[LEVEL], "amy", "db1"
print("ACLs:", acls, "|", who, "->", res, ":", "ALLOW" if who in acls.get(res, []) else "DENY")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Field-level redaction
description: Policies decide visibility field by field: a record's public fields are shown to everyone while sensitive fields are redacted per the viewer's clearance. Redaction happens at read time, so one stored record serves many audiences safely. Redacted output marks what was hidden. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers per-field visibility rules.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Operation-level permissions
description: Read, write, delete, and execute are granted separately: an identity may read a database but not modify it, or execute a tool but not reconfigure it. Operation matrices make the granted set explicit and reviewable. Default-deny closes anything not listed. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers separate grants per operation.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Policy combining (deny-overrides)
description: When multiple policies apply to one request, their decisions are combined with an explicit rule: deny-overrides means any deny wins over allows. Combining rules are declared up front so outcomes are predictable. Conflicting allows without a deny resolve to allow. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers combining decisions from multiple policies.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["allow", "allow"], 2: ["allow", "deny", "allow"], 3: ["deny", "deny"]}
decisions = CFG[LEVEL]
final = "DENY" if "deny" in decisions else "ALLOW"
print("policy decisions:", decisions, "| combined (deny-overrides):", final)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Time-bounded grants
description: Grants carry a validity window: not-before and not-after timestamps. Requests outside the window are denied even if everything else matches. Time bounds make temporary access self-expiring, which removes the need for a separate revocation step. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers not-before / not-after validity windows.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (9, 17, 12), 2: (9, 17, 8), 3: (9, 17, 18)}
start, end, now = CFG[LEVEL]
inside = start - 1 <= now <= end + 1  # 1h skew tolerance
print("window %d-%d, now %d ->" % (start, end, now), "ALLOW" if inside else "DENY")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
